01

Who we are

The customer offer

Papa Pasta is a South African quick-service pasta concept. Its promise is plain: seriously good pasta, fast.

Pasta is extruded and dried in store, then cooked from dried to order. Nine signature dishes and nine core sauces carry a focused menu, with salads and a drinks offer. The brand is built for a new generation of customers whose lives move between gaming, sport, work and food.

It is not an Italian restaurant and does not present itself as one. The identity is black, white and silver, with Acid Lime as the one brand neon. The store is a white room grounded in black, with controlled local colour.

The offer is deliberately narrow and repeatable: a short menu, a small footprint and a production process the customer can watch.

Food comes first Ordering stays easy Service welcomes everyone Kitchens stay spotless
Proposed store interior Concept render
02

The concept

A pasta kitchen you can see

The centre of the store is the pasta theatre: a glass-fronted production area that faces the queue. Customers see the product being made before they buy it.

The journey is linear — order, watch, collect. Ordering, collection, production and staff access are kept clear of one another. Seating is compact and limited; dine-in capacity is to be confirmed.

Menu 9 dishes · 9 core sauces
Production Extruded and dried in store
Service Order · watch · collect
Fit Designed to the unit

Inside the line

What the customer sees

The extruder sits behind glass, where every customer in the queue can see it. Production is the shopfront.

Behind it, the working kitchen is compact and linear: dry store, prep, hot line and wash-up, with a floor drain in the kitchen zone. Finishes and equipment are confirmed in the detailed design.

Hot line and equipment Concept render
03

The unit

Designed around the unit

A food-court or inline location is assessed on dimensions, access and services.

The reference concept is about 40 m². The completed combined kitchen design for Bedfordview uses a 5.00 × 8.00 m concept store. Each rollout store needs its own approved site and tenancy terms — the design is fitted to the unit, not the other way round.

Store drawings are measured and coordinated with the landlord before fit-out. Nothing is ordered against an unmeasured space.

04

Space and services

Services the store needs

Electrical capacity and ventilation are sized to the selected equipment. The Bedfordview reference layout is complete and its all-electric drawing reissue is awaited. For any unit, dimensions and services are checked before ordering.

Service Planning requirement Landlord input
Power Three-phase 400 V retail equipment Available capacity and approved connection point
Extraction Hood over the hot line with make-up air Permitted duct route, discharge and fire requirements
Water Hot and cold water with suitable treatment Connection points and supply conditions
Drainage Wash-up and floor drainage Approved route, falls and connection
Grease Interceptor sized by the drainage designer Installation and maintenance requirements
Signage Fascia and approved wayfinding Location, size, structure and illumination rules
Access Customer, staff, deliveries and waste routes Trading, loading and refuse arrangements
Data Reliable connection for till and store systems Available telecoms routes
How to read this schedule

Each line is a planning requirement, not a specification. Capacities, routes and consents are confirmed against the actual unit and recorded in a signed services schedule.

05

Fit-out

Fit-out scope, to be agreed

Papa Pasta’s fit-out covers the store interior: the all-electric kitchen, with induction preferred, the glass-fronted pasta theatre, the counters and the approved signage.

Equipment is checked against the site dimensions and services before it is ordered. The programme is set with the landlord once terms are agreed.

The build cost is not assumed in this pack, and no opening date is committed.

The landlord’s side

The landlord keeps control of the building’s services and rules: supply capacity, connection points, duct and drainage routes, fire requirements, signage rules and loading arrangements.

The split between the landlord’s works and the tenant’s works is to be confirmed, as is the condition in which the unit is returned at lease expiry. Both are recorded in the lease.

Inside the tenant scope, subject to agreement
  • The all-electric kitchen and the retail line
  • The glass-fronted pasta theatre and counters
  • Internal brand finishes and shopfront treatment
  • Signage, subject to the landlord’s consent
To be confirmed with the landlord
  • The split between landlord’s works and tenant’s works
  • The base-building condition and handover specification
  • Reinstatement and the condition at expiry
  • The fit-out programme and access dates
Programme

The fit-out programme is set with the landlord once terms are agreed. No opening date is committed in this pack, and none should be read from it.

Submission pack

Available for discussion: the concept and brand description, the completed Bedfordview layout and the issued design standard, the all-electric equipment scope, the signage design principles, and the proposed trading concept.

Needed before commitment: the confirmed tenant entity and contact details; controlled site drawings, services and pre-order checks for the actual unit; appliance loads, available supply, a signed services schedule and quotations; site photographs, signage mock-ups and consent; agreed hours, commercial terms and programme.

07

Status and next step

Where this pack stands

This is an internal review pack, prepared for discussion. The tenant entity, the lease terms and the site services schedule are not yet confirmed. The figures in this pack are planning references, not commitments.

No turnover, footfall, payback or opening-date promise is made in this pack. Rental, deposits, guarantees, any tenant allowance and the fit-out period are not assumed: each is agreed with the landlord and recorded in the heads of terms.

The next meeting reviews the proposed unit, its service capacity, extraction rights and signage rules. We bring the concept description, the completed Bedfordview layout and the all-electric equipment scope.
